Spatial Desktop design system

Material follows interaction.

Opaque ABS gives pointer-driven controls a physical body and uses discrete LED lamps for state. Edge-lit acrylic carries temporary, ambient and system information through illuminated engraving. Neither material is decoration: each one explains how an element behaves before it is used.

1
Role chooses materialPersistent and physical uses ABS. Transient and ambient uses glass.
2
State chooses lightPersistent light belongs only to toggles, selections and progress.
3
Object chooses shapeDesktop Areas are square. Movable app windows are squircles.

Philosophy

A small set of rules should explain the whole interface.

01
Tactile, not ornamental

Depth must communicate pressability, insertion or stacking. Flat information stays flat.

Input-device honesty

Desktop controls echo mouse and keyboard switches. Touch controls belong to the continuous phone-glass surface.

One depth step

A surface can be raised, level or recessed. Avoid nesting multiple embossed frames around content.

Solid working content

The main content of every app window is always opaque and readable. Glass never sits behind long-form content.

Light carries meaning

App colour marks focus, selection, progress and an active toggle—not every border and icon.

Fast mechanical motion

Buttons move down in 8 ms and release in 16 ms. Toggle buttons click equally fast, then remain physically held.

Two materials, two jobs

Mix them only at a deliberate boundary.

02
ABS plasticDurable · physical · opaque

ABS is the body of applications and controls manipulated with a pointer. It should feel like the shell and buttons of a well-made mouse.

  • Movable application windows
  • Push and toggle buttons on ABS
  • Toolbars, tabs and window chrome
  • Solid application content surfaces
Never make primary reading or working content transparent.
Edge-lit acrylic glassAcrylight · ambient · contextual

“Glass” is one continuous acrylic sheet, not a pile of translucent capsules. Neutral parallel reflections reveal its cut thickness; hidden edge emitters feed light into engraved or frosted marks only where state must be communicated.

  • Docked Apps, Project and System Areas
  • Context menus, popovers and toasts
  • Overview and search surfaces
  • Small displays inserted into ABS
Keep the clear face quiet. Colour belongs to injection points and scattering marks—not the whole perimeter.

Light behaves differently

The same colour can communicate state through two different physical models.

03
ABS plastic

ABS uses a restrained state light

Match the real Dolphin controls in the desktop demo: a flat two-pixel application-colour trace with one short halo. It sits flush in the ABS surface, with no contrasting bezel, white centre or extra luminous body.

Emitter
Local indicator integrated flush with the control
Light form
Flat two-pixel line or three-pixel vertical slit
App colour
Application primary colour without whitening
Bloom
One restrained six-pixel shadow at 56%
Inactive
A faint neutral state rail only where required
Edge-lit acrylic

Acrylight reveals a path, not a glowing panel

Hidden LEDs inject light at short sections of the cut edge. Total internal reflection keeps the face transparent; only an engraving, frosted groove or locally exposed edge scatters the light toward the user.

Emitter
Short concealed injection points along the outer edge
Thickness
Neutral parallel reflections reveal the cut panel
Light path
Travels invisibly inside the clear sheet
App colour
Appears only at injection points and scattering marks
Bloom
One sharp core with a four-pixel local scatter
Inactive
The etched groove remains faintly visible but unlit
Shared meaning, different construction: coloured light means active state, selection, focus or progress. ABS exposes a local state indicator. Acrylic transports light through one sheet and releases it only from an engraving, frost or exposed injection edge. Neither material should glow as an undifferentiated surface.

State light is a language

The coloured line is not decoration. Its shape, duration and intensity describe the control state.

Toggle buttons

Pressing and toggling are separate events. Every button performs the same fast 8 ms click. After it resolves, an ABS toggle stays lower and powers its indicator; a glass toggle remains in the shared sheet while its engraved mark stays lit. A push button retains neither.

Sliders

The light represents a value, so it ends exactly at the thumb and follows without easing. ABS reuses the same two-pixel state trace as the active Dolphin tab; the remaining distance is a thin neutral guide. Glass brightens a frosted groove in the acrylic sheet.

Colour ownership

Use the application primary colour for in-app state. System surfaces use their owning Area colour. Warning, error and success colours replace it only when status meaning is more important than app identity.

Where the light may exist

ABS light may appear only as the shared state trace, a small dot, a vertical slit or a backlit symbol—never as glowing plastic. Acrylight may appear only at an outer injection edge or where the shared sheet is engraved, frosted or cut.

Every component in both materials

The behaviour stays consistent. Only the physical response changes.

Composition rules

How the pieces combine without becoming busy.

06

Do

  • Keep app content fully opaque.
  • Use one dominant material per surface.
  • Reserve app colour for meaningful state.
  • Let empty space separate groups.
  • Keep borders thin and local.
  • Use real app icons in launch surfaces.

Do not

  • Put ABS buttons on a glass sheet.
  • Wrap every item in a raised card.
  • Give push buttons persistent light.
  • Blur text-heavy content over wallpaper.
  • Stack border inside border inside border.
  • Use glow merely to decorate an edge.

Recommended defaults. Scale spatial values, not interaction timing.

Implementation templates

Minimal patterns developers can adapt without changing the semantics.

08
Matching ABS and glass buttons
<div class="surface abs">
  <button class="button abs-button">Push action</button>
</div>

<div class="surface glass">
  <button class="button glass-button">Push action</button>
</div>

<button class="abs-button toggle-button" aria-pressed="true">
  Toggle action
</button>

/* Same ON state; two physically different emitters. */
.abs-button[aria-pressed="true"] .light-bar {
  height: 2px;
  border-radius: 2px;
  background: var(--app-primary);
  box-shadow: var(--abs-led-bloom);
}
.glass-button[aria-pressed="true"] .engraving {
  height: 1px;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--app-primary) 82%, white 18%);
  box-shadow: var(--acrylic-etch-bloom);
}
.glass-button:not([aria-pressed="true"]) .engraving {
  background: var(--glass-groove);     /* visible etch, no emitted colour */
  box-shadow: none;
}
Matching ABS and glass sliders
<!-- Same value and semantics; different physical rendering. -->
<input class="range abs-range" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="42">
<input class="range glass-range" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="42">

.abs-range .track {
  height: 2px;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 28%, transparent);
}
.abs-range .filled-part {
  height: 2px;
  border-radius: 2px;
  background: var(--app-primary);
  box-shadow: var(--abs-led-bloom);
}
.glass-range .filled-part {
  height: 1px;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--app-primary) 82%, white 18%);
  box-shadow: var(--acrylic-etch-bloom);
}
.glass-range .thumb {
  border: 1px solid var(--glass-edge);
  border-radius: 2px;
  background: transparent;
  box-shadow: var(--acrylic-edge-stack);
}
Glass context menu
<menu class="glass context-menu">
  <button class="menu-row">Move to Project</button>
  <button class="menu-row">Keep visible</button>
</menu>

.context-menu {
  border-radius: 0;                 /* desktop structure */
  background: var(--glass-surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--glass-edge);
  box-shadow: var(--acrylic-edge-stack);
  backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(1.08);
}
.menu-row {
  background: transparent;         /* rows are not separate glass buttons */
  border: 0;
  box-shadow: none;
}
Solid app with a glass insert
<article class="app-window abs">
  <header class="app-titlebar">Dolphin</header>
  <div class="glass recessed-field">Downloads</div>
  <main class="app-content solid">...files...</main>
</article>

/* The content is always opaque—even when the toolbar contains glass. */
.app-content { background: var(--app-content); opacity: 1; }
